name: Calcium polystyrene sulfonate
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero
summary: Calcium polystyrene sulfonate is a non-absorbed resin that exchanges calcium for potassium in the gut (about 0.7 mmol potassium per gram). The Irish label indicates it for hyperkalemia in acute and chronic kidney insufficiency, including dialysis, so no kidney dose change applies; dosing follows serum potassium. It is not effective enough alone for potassium above 6.5 mmol/L or ECG changes. It has no US FDA label.
kidney_function_basis: Not renally cleared; dose is titrated to serum potassium. Bands shown on creatinine clearance (CrCl).

bands.recommendation: Kidney-indicated drug; dose is set by serum potassium, not kidney function: 20 g orally 1 to 3 times daily in about 150 mL liquid with food, or 40 g rectally 1 to 3 times daily; stop at potassium 5 mmol/L (SmPC).

hd: Indicated in dialysis patients; same dosing by potassium (SmPC). Not a substitute for dialysis in severe hyperkalemia.
pd: Same dosing by potassium (SmPC indication includes dialysis).
crrt: Same dosing if gut function allows; avoid with reduced gut motility or ileus (contraindicated).
monitoring: Serum potassium (stop at 5 mmol/L), calcium (hypercalcemia, especially with calcium binders or vitamin D analogues) and magnesium. Constipation (stop if significant); never give with sorbitol (colonic necrosis). Separate from antacids or laxatives by at least 3 hours (SmPC 4.2, 4.4).

pediatric.approved_ages: Children; not for oral use in neonates (SmPC).
pediatric.usual_dose: Children: 0.5 to 1 g/kg/day orally in at least 3 divided doses; rectal dose at least as large when oral is not possible (SmPC).
pediatric.notes: Neonates: no oral use; no use by any route with reduced gut motility. Fecal impaction after rectal use in children reported.

renal.recommendation: Dose by potassium: 0.5 to 1 g/kg/day in 3 or more divided doses (SmPC).
